body.estimand_functional: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\). For each finite query the field-theoretic minimal polynomial \(p_e(t)\) exists uniquely; its uniform fixed-parameter rational-circuit construction is conditional on a valid source-prime chart package.

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The estimation layer uses independent observational sampling at fixed \(G,n\).
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal query is the direct structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: When \(d_e(G)<\infty\) and a valid bounded source-prime chart package has been supplied, project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the resulting regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the conditionally constructed certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. When \(d_e(G)=\infty\), the unconditional symbolic stage reports transcendence and the finite-set inference rung does not apply. Without the chart package, the unconditional finite tag does not by itself supply an estimator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for tree-shaped linear SEMs; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness, while Gupta--Bläser later established the complete per-edge \(1/2/\infty\) classification and Briefs--Bläser reports the corresponding faster implementation.
Theorem 27 gives the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) trichotomy for rooted directed trees and therefore the finite-degree upper boundary two.
Theorem 1 gives an \(O(n^3\log^2 n)\) randomized implementation of the same complete tree-only \(1/2/\infty\) predicate.
The paper gives graphical identifiability criteria, full-fiber mixed-component decomposition, and small-graph finite-degree computations.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification of coefficients from ancestral induced subgraphs to the full graph.

Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space. The unconditional theorem here gives a source-rank finite-versus-transcendental certificate on the tree-plus-excess class, but exact finite eliminant output remains conditional.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 search for minimum bounded-degree rational identifying formulas, not algebraic coordinate minimal polynomials or branch degree.

Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation for generically zero-dimensional parametric systems and controls specialization bad loci, but it does not select the SEM source-prime chart required by the conditional corollary.
The paper computes separating forms, rational univariate representations, isolating boxes, and exact signs for bivariate polynomial systems.
The paper derives consistency, rates, and confidence regions for criterion-defined identified sets.
The preprint derives influence functions, asymptotic normality, and Wald inference for rational half-trek estimators.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior and analyzes explicit degree-two failures of injectivity.

body.tldr: Adding a bounded number of parents to a supplied rooted directed tree creates a finite algebraic ambiguity regime not summarized by whole-fiber cardinality. The focal object remains the sharp single-coordinate complex degree frontier \(D_k(n)\). The paper proves the projection-aware upper bound and pursues the all-size attaining recurrence. Algorithmically, a source-Jacobian rank comparison gives an unconditional fixed-parameter finite-versus-transcendental tag and a dominance certificate. Exact finite degrees, minimal polynomials, bad-locus circuits, real lifting, and the regular finite-set inference rung are obtained conditionally when a bounded reduced chart of the embedded source prime is supplied; constructing that chart uniformly is a named open question rather than an implicit elimination step.

project_justification.gap: Existing tree algorithms and general mixed-graph work study identification decisions, rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination. No result determines the maximum finite extension degree of one directed coefficient as a function of both graph size and the number of extra parents.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which ordinary vertices retain Möbius structure while at most \(2k\) exceptional incoming coefficients form a coupled quadratic core. The hard boundary is whether constrained covariance coefficients realize the multihomogeneous orientation count at every smaller size.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the projection-aware degree bound and all-size frontier program, proves an unconditional fixed-parameter algebraic-versus-transcendental rank certificate, and isolates the precise source-prime chart needed for exact finite eliminants. A conditional geometric-resolution theorem then yields the minimal polynomial, specialization and lifting circuits, and the regular finite-set inference interface, while a named open question records the missing uniform chart-selection and descent theorem.

body.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for tree-shaped linear SEMs; Gupta and Bläser later established the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) classification, and Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree predicate in fasttreeid. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton exhibit higher-degree small SEMs, so novelty is not attached to a lone cubic or quartic. Dörfler, van der Zander, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz give a general polynomial-space generic identification decision, while Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different notion from algebraic branch degree. The unconditional theorem here is correspondingly limited to a parameterized source-rank finite-versus-transcendental tag. Corniquel and the geometric-resolution algorithms of Giusti--Lecerf--Salvy and Lecerf justify finite solving and specialization after a reduced regular-sequence chart or lifting fiber is supplied; they do not select the embedded SEM source prime from an extensional quadratic core or perform descent for an unspecified component. Exact degree, minimal-polynomial, and exceptional-set output is therefore stated as a conditional corollary plus an explicit open chart-selection question. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer and Mareis, Sturma, and Drton inform the downstream regular inference architecture, which is likewise conditional on those symbolic outputs.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The quadratic core preserves the queried projection extensionally but does not present the reduced embedded source prime. Its displayed equations may vanish to higher order along that component, so source-parametric identity testing cannot manufacture a nonzero conormal Jacobian minor. General radical decomposition, a generic rational univariate representation, and lifting-fiber algorithms do not establish the required chart selection or coefficient descent in \(n^{C(k+1)}\) complexity. The orientation coefficient remains only an upper envelope until the separate all-size realization problem is solved. Coordinate localization is not promoted to full-fiber equality; real roots are not equated with real supported lifts; and local Jacobian rank is not used to claim real uniqueness.
body.honest_scope: The all-size frontier recurrence and its attaining families remain the identification kernel. Unconditionally, the algorithmic contribution is a randomized exact source-Jacobian comparison returning either \(\mathtt{algebraic}\) with the established bound \(d_e(G)\leq2^{k+1}\), or \(\infty\) with a dominance certificate; it returns no finite degree, eliminant, or bad-locus circuit. Conditional on a supplied bounded reduced source-prime chart and source-nonzero Jacobian minor for every recorded stratum, localized geometric resolution returns \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), and \(h_{G,e}\) with explicit dependence on chart size and intermediate geometric degree. Exceptional-set validity, real lifting, root-\(m\) finite-set inference, and singleton asymptotic normality are asserted only under that conditional symbolic output. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, all-singular-covariance guarantee, or inference from complex degree to real uniqueness is claimed.
body.interpretation: The unconditional certificate answers whether the queried edge has finite complex algebraic ambiguity or a Zariski-dense infinite coordinate image; it does not enumerate finite branches. A valid reduced source-prime chart upgrades the finite tag to the exact field degree and monic branch polynomial. Real roots are retained only after a supported real-extension test, and statistical neighborhoods cover all retained simple branches without selecting among them.
